title: Where do you live?
title_target: Где ты живёшь? — Gde ty zhivyosh?
goal: Talk about places: city, home, office, campus. And master the prepositional case — the ending that appears every time a noun follows "in" or "at".
bekal: answer Где вы живёте? and Где вы работаете?
name the parts of a home and public places

dialogs.title: Диалог — Looking for an apartment
dialogs.intro: Ani wants to move out of the dorm. She asks Сергей, her neighbor from Unit 5. Notice that every noun after в and на changes its ending to -е.

lines.speaker: Сергей:
lines.id: In this building, on the fifth floor. Why?
lines.literal: in — this — building, on — fifth — floor. and — why?

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: I'm looking for an apartment. The dorm is noisy.
lines.literal: I — look-for — apartment. in — dorm — noisy.

lines.speaker: Сергей:
lines.id: I see. There are good apartments in our area.
lines.literal: understand-I. in — our — district — are — good — apartments.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Is it far from the university?

lines.speaker: Сергей:
lines.id: No, it's close. Fifteen minutes by metro.
lines.literal: no, close. fifteen — minutes — on — metro.

lines.speaker: Сергей:
lines.id: Everything's nearby. The shop is on the corner, the pharmacy across the street.
lines.literal: all — nearby. shop — on — corner, pharmacy — opposite.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Sounds great. How much does an apartment cost here?
lines.literal: sounds — great. how-much — costs — apartment — here?

lines.speaker: Сергей:
lines.id: A one-room place is about forty thousand a month.
lines.literal: one-room — about — forty — thousand — in — month.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Hmm. Maybe the dorm isn't that noisy after all.
lines.literal: hmm. maybe — then, in — dorm — not — so — noisy.

notes: **After в and на meaning location, the noun changes its ending to -е.** ⚠️ Москва → в Москв**е**, дом → в дом**е**, работа → на работ**е**, стол → на стол**е**. That's the prepositional case, and it's named that because it **only** ever appears after a preposition — never on its own.

**The ending is almost always -е, which makes this the easiest case.** Masculine, feminine, neuter: all **-е**. The only exceptions are words ending in **-ия/-ие** (Россия → в Росси**и**, общежитие → в общежити**и**) and a few masculine words that take a stressed **-у** (в углу, в саду, в аэропорту).

**В means "in", на means "on" — but part of the real split has to be memorized.** *в доме* (in the house), *на столе* (on the table) make sense. But *на работе* (at work), *на почте* (at the post office), *на вокзале* (at the station) can't be explained with "on". English has the same kind of quirks ("on the bus", "at work"). The grammar box below has the list to learn.

**⚠️ Don't confuse this with в + accusative.** *Я живу в Москв**е*** (I live in Moscow, prepositional) but *Я еду в Москв**у*** (I'm going to Moscow, accusative). The preposition is exactly the same; only the noun ending differs — and the meaning switches from "in" to "to". Unit 13 covers this fully; for now just know that **-е means staying put**.

**Далеко от and близко от take the genitive.** *далеко от университет**а*** (far from the university), *близко от дом**а*** (close to home). The preposition **от** is always followed by the genitive, just like из and без.

**Однокомнатная квартира means a one-room apartment** — and in Russia the count doesn't include the kitchen. Однокомнатная = one room plus kitchen plus bathroom. Двухкомнатная = two rooms. ⚠️ Not the same as the English "two-bedroom": a Russian двухкомнатная often has just one bedroom plus a living room.
**Может быть means "maybe", and is often shortened to just может.** *Может, завтра?* — maybe tomorrow?

grammars.title: Prepositional — the -е ending for nearly everything

head: Dictionary form
Prepositional
Example
rows: Я в доме. — I'm in the house.
Книга на столе. — The book is on the table.
Он на работе. — He's at work.
в угл**у**, в сад**у**, в аэропорт**у**

after: This case is also used for "about": *Мы говорим **о работе*** — we're talking about work. *Книга **о России*** — a book about Russia.
⚠️ The preposition **о** becomes **об** before a vowel: *об Ани*, *об Италии*. Just to make it easier to say — like English "a" becoming "an".

grammars.title: В or на — the list to learn
body: For most enclosed places, use **в**. The list below shows places that take **на** even though the logic isn't obvious.

head: Takes В
Takes НА ⚠️
rows: на почте — at the post office
на вокзале — at the train station
на остановке — at the bus stop
на улице — in the street, outside

after: No single rule explains the whole right-hand column. A pattern that helps a bit: **на** is used for places pictured as an open area or an activity (улица, площадь, урок, концерт), while **в** is for enclosed spaces. The rest is memorization.

Mistakes here don't kill communication — *в работе* will still be understood — but they instantly mark you as a foreigner. Learn those ten right-hand rows and you've covered most everyday conversations.

blocks.title: Place words that need no preposition
items: **дома** (*DO-ma*) — at home. Not *в доме*: if you mean "being at home" (rather than "inside the house building"), the word is дома. *Я дома* — I'm at home.
**здесь / там / тут** — here / there / here (casual). Never need a preposition.
**рядом** (*RYA-dam*) — next door, very close. *Магазин рядом* — the shop is close by.
**напротив** (*na-PRO-tif*) — opposite, across the street. Takes the genitive when you say opposite what: *напротив дом**а***.
⚠️ **домой** (*da-MOY*) is different from **дома**: домой means "(to) home", дома means "at home". *Я иду домой* — I'm going home. *Я дома* — I'm at home.
